oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer grant authenticates service accounts/machine identities rather than end-user browser sessions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not compare machine-token identity behavior to interactive user-login expectations.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims only according to granted scopes; many profile and email fields are omitted unless explicitly requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing optional claims is by design and should not be flagged as identity loss or authorization failure.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo only returns information depending on the granted scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of email/profile/roles/metadata claims without corresponding scopes is by design and must not be treated as identity confusion or authorization stripping.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange may return opaque or JWT access tokens, and id_token is only returned with openid scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Differences in token format or absence of id_token are by design and should not be treated as privilege anomalies.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange may return invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds what was granted by the resource owner.
oidc_jwt.note: This is correct authorization binding, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Access tokens include all client IDs and the project ID in aud by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat extra default audience entries as audience escalation without first accounting for documented defaults.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer assertions are documented as signed JWTs sent to the token endpoint, but the docs do not describe jti tracking or one-time-use enforcement for authorization-grant assertions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability based on these docs alone; treat as stateless JWT behavior unless a stronger one-time-use guarantee is documented.

oidc_jwt.description: redirect_uri must match exactly one of the preregistered URIs and, for code exchange, must match exactly the redirect_uri used in the authorization request.
oidc_jwt.note: Failures on mismatched redirect_uri are expected and should not be reported as flow incoherence.

oidc_jwt.description: Invalid response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored.
oidc_jwt.note: A flow continuing with default response handling after an invalid response_mode is documented behavior, not a coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo endpoint returns ZITADEL's internal subject identifier in sub rather than echoing an external login name or JWT assertion label.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid false I4 positives when the sent identifier is a service-account userId, clientId, or external username string.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion itself must carry time claims acceptable to ZITADEL: aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain, exp must be in the future for control tokens, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Without a valid control, LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed assertion construction rather than freshness enforcement.

For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT header must include kid matching the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL uses kid to identify the verification key. A missing or wrong kid can cause rejection before the intended signature-validation test is exercised.

For I1 issuer/audience trust tests on login_with_jwt, the assertion aud claim is exact-value based and MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain as documented. Do not use wildcard or pattern values; there is no companion matching-mode parameter. If testing multiple issuers/audiences, generate distinct exact assertions rather than assuming glob semantics.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests in the authorization-code flow, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL requires an exact match and returns invalid_grant when the redirection URI differs. This is by-spec flow binding, not an identity bug.

For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send other PKCE methods when constructing control flows. A failing exchange with a non-S256 method is invalid test setup, not evidence about code/session binding.

For I3 state-swap tests, start_oidc_auth SHOULD include state and the oracle must evaluate callback/code binding rather than identity comparison alone. ZITADEL documents state as the CSRF/session continuity value returned unmodified to the redirect_uri; omitting it weakens the test and can create ambiguous results.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, token_exchange audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is expected by design. Use a control exchange where audience is within the documented subset before asserting any audience-binding weakness.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope at token_exchange may be reduced or rejected when it exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. Always compare against a control exchange with equal-or-narrower scope; do not treat rejection of broader scope as a vulnerability.

For I5 token-exchange type tests, only documented token-type combinations are valid. In particular, subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type=jwt is only meaningful for the documented combinations. Invalid type combinations must not be interpreted as authorization-binding failures.

For SESSION inspection after login_with_jwt, verify_granted_identity uses /oidc/v1/userinfo and requires a user access token. The docs explicitly say to send the access_token of the user, not the client. JWT bearer service-account tokens may not yield human-user style claims at userinfo, so absence of expected profile fields is not by itself an I4 violation; rely on sub and returned claims actually documented for the granted scopes.

For I5 claim-presence tests, many claims are scope-gated in ZITADEL. UserInfo and token contents depend on requested scopes such as openid, profile, email, offline_access, and reserved urn:zitadel scopes. Missing claims without the corresponding scope are expected behavior, not under-grant or over-grant evidence. Always request the exact scope needed for the claim under test.

For I5 reserved-scope audience tests, adding urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud or urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud intentionally adds audience values to the access token. Do not include these scopes in baseline/control flows unless the test specifically targets audience expansion, or you may create false positives about excess audience grants.

For revoke_session, the documented revocation endpoint requires client authentication depending on the authorization method. A bare token POST may fail with invalid_client. Treat revocation as supported only when the test harness can supply the appropriate client authentication for the token being revoked; otherwise cleanup failure is environmental, not a session-lifecycle bug.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. A failure without these baseline claims is invalid test setup, not evidence about exp/nbf enforcement.

For I1 key-identification tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT header MUST include kid matching the downloaded keyId. Missing or wrong kid can fail before the platform reaches the intended trust/signature validation path.

For I2 token-freshness tests on login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid assertion alongside the ATTACK login. Recommended control claims: iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Without a control, token rejection cannot be distinguished from broken client/service-account setup.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests on exchange_code_for_token, ZITADEL requires redirect_uri at the token endpoint to match exactly the redirect_uri used at authorization time. Any mismatch is expected invalid_grant behavior, not a session mixup or identity bug.

For I3 PKCE tests, when code_challenge was sent on start_oidc_auth, exchange_code_for_token MUST send client_id and the matching code_verifier. ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Tests using other methods are invalid setup.

For I3 state-swap tests, state is only returned to the redirect_uri and is recommended for CSRF mitigation. The executor must compare returned state values at the browser redirect boundary; the token endpoint does not validate state directly.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, token_exchange audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected rejection and must not be reported as inconsistent authorization behavior.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, ZITADEL documents that invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. The fuzzer MUST request expanded scope only after establishing a narrower baseline token, and interpret invalid_scope as correct enforcement.

For token_exchange type tests, supported token-type combinations are constrained: subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type=jwt is only for specific combinations documented in the token type matrix. Unsupported combinations are invalid setup, not security findings.

For verify_granted_identity, UserInfo returns claims depending on granted scopes. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes during login before asserting presence/absence of claims such as email, profile fields, roles, or metadata. Missing claims without corresponding scope are expected behavior.

For revocation tests, /oauth/v2/revoke requires client authentication depending on the configured auth method. The fuzzer MUST supply the appropriate client credentials or client assertion when revoking; otherwise failure may be invalid_client rather than evidence that revocation is unsupported.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp and iat claims, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use template values such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control tokens. Without a valid control assertion, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken JWT construction.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 issuer/audience trust tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}). Tokens with other audiences are expected to fail by design, so do not interpret such failures as proof of signature or issuer enforcement beyond audience validation.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 key-identification tests, JWTs used with the JWT profile or private_key_jwt client authentication MUST carry a kid header matching the downloaded keyId. Missing or mismatched kid can fail before any deeper signature-validation logic is exercised.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token against login_with_jwt, do NOT flag successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability unless the docs explicitly promise one-time-use semantics. The provided documentation describes stateless JWT bearer validation requirements (signature, issuer, expiry) and does not document jti tracking or single-use enforcement.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used at start_oidc_auth. A mismatch is expected to return invalid_grant by design and should be asserted as flow binding, not treated as an identity mismatch.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx authorization code grant; authmethods/_basic.mdx; authmethods/_pkce.mdx; authmethods/_jwtpk.mdx

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 PKCE tests, when start_oidc_auth includes code_challenge, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the matching code_verifier and client_id. ZITADEL documents S256 as the only supported code_challenge_method. Using another method or omitting code_verifier after sending a challenge is expected to fail by design.

For I3 state-swap tests, start_oidc_auth SHOULD include a state value and the oracle must validate callback state continuity. Omitting state weakens the test because ZITADEL only recommends state for CSRF mitigation; a missing state is not evidence of broken session binding.

For I5 scope-tightening and token-exchange escalation tests, token_exchange audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design and should not be interpreted as broader authorization bugs.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, requested scope on token_exchange may be rejected with invalid_scope when it exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. This is by design per the token endpoint error semantics; compare exchanged claims only when the exchange succeeds.

For I5 token type tests on token_exchange, respect ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type jwt is only valid for specific combinations; user_id subject_token is only allowed with actor_token. Invalid combinations are expected setup failures, not vulnerabilities.

For I5 audience tests, ZITADEL's access-token aud claim by default includes all client IDs and the project ID. Do not assume a single audience value in baseline tokens; when testing audience narrowing or wrong-audience exchange, inspect the actual aud set first.

For I5 org-binding tests via OIDC authorization, reserved scopes have enforcement semantics: urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces membership in the selected organization, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces membership plus username suffix. Failures under these scopes are expected policy enforcement, not identity confusion.

For I4 identity verification, verify_granted_identity returns sub as ZITADEL's internal subject identifier, not the original external username or service-account label. The fuzzer MUST compare stable identity claims/metadata with this in mind and MUST NOT expect the sent JWT subject string to be echoed by /userinfo.
